 Election 2026: Your Guide to Voting in Chesterfield
 Chesterfield on Point
 Posted on October 20, 2026 
 Do you have questions about voting in Chesterfield County? With Election Day coming up on Tuesday, Nov. 3, here's what you need to know about casting your ballot this fall.
 Can I vote while attending college, or do I have to return home? 
 College students should confirm where they are registered to vote. Students may choose to register at their home address or at their college residence, but they cannot be registered to vote in both locations. Instead, they should decide where they want to register and vote accordingly.
 Can I vote on Election Day if I am not registered? 
 Virginia allows same-day voter registration. Those who are eligible may register and cast a provisional ballot on Election Day. These ballots are then reviewed by the Electoral Board after the election to determine whether they can be counted.
 Voters should register or update their registration before the applicable deadline whenever possible.
 Can I submit my ballot online or by text message? 
 No, ballots cannot be submitted online or by text message. In Chesterfield County, there are three ways for eligible voters to vote: by absentee ballot by mail, early in person, or in person on Election Day at their assigned polling place.
 Is my voter registration card the only identification I can use to vote? 
 No. Virginia accepts several forms of identification at polling places and early voting locations, including:
 Virginia DMV-issued driver’s license
 Valid U.S. passport
 Voter confirmation documents
 Government-issued identification cards
 Student identification cards issued by eligible U.S. colleges and universities or Virginia public and private schools
 Employer-issued photo ID
 A current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or other qualifying government document showing your name and address
 An ID Confirmation Statement
 Voters who do not have an acceptable form of identification may be offered an ID Confirmation Statement to complete and sign. This will serve as the acceptable form of ID. If the voter refuses to sign this form, a provisional ballot will be offered.
 Voters must have until noon the third business day after the election to present an acceptable form of identification to the General Register or Electoral Board for the provisional ballot to be counted. For the most current list of acceptable identification, visit the Virginia Department of Elections website.
 Does the U.S. Postal Service determine whether my mailed ballot will be counted? 
 No. The U.S. Postal Service delivers election mail through its standard procedures. It does not determine voter eligibility or decide whether a ballot will be counted.
 Election officials maintain voter registration records, issue ballots and determine whether returned ballots meet Virginia’s requirements. Voters should use the return envelope provided, follow all instructions and return their ballots by the applicable deadlines.
 Do I have to register to vote in person? 
 No. Eligible Virginia residents can register to vote online, by mail or in person. Voters can also update their registration through available methods.
 Virginia also permits same-day registration, which allows eligible individuals to register and vote using a provisional ballot. Voters are encouraged to register or update their information before the applicable deadline.
 Can I vote if I serve as an Officer of Election? 
 Yes. Officers of Election are eligible to vote. They may vote early in person or by absentee ballot, following the applicable procedures and deadlines. If the Officer of Election is serving at their home precinct election day, the OOE may vote in person on Election Day.
 Will my vote count if I return my ballot by mail? 
 Yes, provided your ballot meets Virginia’s requirements for counting. Generally, ballots received by noon on the third business day after Election Day may be counted if they were received by 7 p.m. on Election Day or postmarked on or before Election Day. Ballots postmarked after Election Day will not be counted.
 Voters should follow the instructions included with their ballot and return it as early as possible.
 Do I have to register with a political party in Virginia? 
 No. Virginia voters do not register by political party. During a primary election, voters may be asked to choose either a Democratic or Republican ballot when both parties hold primaries. A voter may participate in only one party’s primary during a dual-party primary election.
 Will I receive the same ballot during early voting as I would on Election Day? 
 Yes. Voters receive the same ballot for their election district whether they vote absentee by mail, early in person or in person on Election Day.
 Can I change my mind and vote again after casting my ballot? 
 No. Once you cast your ballot, you cannot vote again in that election. This applies whether you vote absentee by mail, early in person or in person on Election Day.
 A ballot is considered cast once it is deposited into the ballot-counting machine or, for a mailed ballot, the designated ballot drop box.
 Are absentee and provisional ballots counted only if an election is close? 
 No. Absentee ballots and in-person ballots are counted according to Virginia election law, regardless of how close the race is. Provisional ballots are reviewed to determine whether they meet the requirements to be counted.
 Can I vote during early voting and then vote again on Election Day? 
 No. Registered voters may vote only once in an election. You can choose to vote absentee by mail, vote early in person or vote at your assigned polling place on Election Day.
 Important Election Dates and Information 
 Early voting : Sept. 18–Oct. 31, 2026
 Voter registration deadline : Friday, Oct. 23, 2026
 Election Day : Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026
 Early voting locations and hours : Visit chesterfield.gov/registrar for locations, schedules and additional details.
 Election Day voting hours : Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters in line by 7 p.m. may cast their ballots.
 Find your polling place : Check your voter registration and assigned polling place before Election Day through the Virginia Department of Elections Citizen Portal .
 For more information about registering to vote, early voting, acceptable identification and absentee ballots, visit chesterfield.gov/registrar or call (804) 748-1471.
